steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: On 23 August 1939, Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union signed a non-aggression pact in Moscow. The public agreement promised that neither side would attack the other for 10 years. A secret protocol divided eastern Europe into spheres of influence: Germany would get western Poland, and the USSR would get eastern Poland, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, and Bessarabia. This pact shocked the world - the two ideological enemies had made a deal.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: At 4:45 am on 1 September 1939, the German battleship Schleswig-Holstein opened fire on the Polish garrison at Westerplatte in Danzig. Over 1.5 million German troops, with 2,500 tanks and 1,900 aircraft, invaded Poland from the north, south, and west. The attack used the "Blitzkrieg" (lightning war) tactic of rapid armoured advances supported by overwhelming air power.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: On 3 September 1939, Britain declared war on Germany at 11:15 am, followed by France at 5:00 pm. Chamberlain broadcast to the nation: "This country is at war with Germany." The Second World War had begun. However, the declaration came two days after the invasion - there had been delays while Britain and France made last-minute attempts to negotiate.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Appeasement was abandoned because Hitler's actions after Munich proved he could not be trusted and his aims were conquest, not self-determination. The seizure of Czechoslovakia (March 1939) was the decisive moment that turned British opinion against further concessions.
